data.name: PanMainInfo1
data.value: Pan is Arcadia’s controller guard. It makes sure Arcadia can use every controller to the full, and decides how other launchers, games and programs deal with them. Pan does this by “hiding” your controllers from other programs and games and creating a virtual copy of them instead, which Pan controls.

data.name: PanOffInfo
data.value: Other programs and games see your real controllers. Arcadia doesn’t create any virtual controllers.

data.name: PanOnInfo
data.value: Pan hides your controllers from other programs and games and controls their virtual copies instead.

data.name: PanMainInfo2
data.value: This way, Arcadia features such as mouse mode or “Back to Arcadia” work everywhere without other launchers reacting to them too, such as Steam’s desktop layout. Arcadia becomes the control center for your controllers. Pan makes sure real and virtual controllers work together without errors, and gives your controllers back at once, for example if Arcadia ends unexpectedly.

data.name: PanMainInfo3
data.value: Pan also lets you assign any virtual controller to your real controllers. That way you can use controllers in games that otherwise don’t support them, for example the Steam Controller.

data.name: PanMainInfo4
data.value: Out of the box, the Steam Controller only works as a real controller in Steam.
